title: Floodgate sweep heuristics — personal probe notes
content:
Goal: quick synthetic + replayed arrival sweep to understand what heuristics reduce p99 during coordinated client "floodgate" opens (many clients transitioning from idle to active within 1-10s).

Short summary:
- Primary hypothesis: small, staggered prewarm + adaptive prefix priming reduces p99 without large cost.
- Secondary: increasing batch timeout reduces p50 but can worsen p99 under extreme concurrency; hybrid (short timeout + opportunistic coalescing) looks promising.

Environment & model:
- cluster: dev-dedicated-us-west (4xA100 share), serving-runtime branch floodgate-experiments
- model: redwood-13b-quant (int4), seq len=1024, kv-cache enabled
- client: replay trace generated from production-tails (scale factor x2) + synthetic Poisson bursts (lambda varied)

Important configs tested (representative):
1) baseline: no prewarm, batch_timeout_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=4096, dynamic_batch=true
2) prewarm-eager: client sends 1 warm probe per shard before ramp, batch_timeout_ms=8
3) staggered-prewarm: clients randomized 0-3000ms prewarm offsets
4) adaptive-priming: if cache_miss_rate > 0.2, send prefix priming request for common prompts
5) long-timeout: batch_timeout_ms=30, otherwise same as baseline

Commands used (local harness):
- run_replay.sh --trace replay.json --clients 120 --ramp 5s --duration 180s --batch-timeout 8
- metrics export to csv: p50,p95,p99,goodput(qps),gpu_util,kv_hit

Representative results (synth averaged, 3 runs):
- baseline: p50=62ms, p95=210ms, p99=870ms, qps=410, gpu_util=68%, kv_hit=0.11
- prewarm-eager: p50=66ms, p95=190ms, p99=420ms, qps=395, gpu_util=64%, kv_hit=0.23
- staggered-prewarm: p50=64ms, p95=180ms, p99=260ms, qps=400, gpu_util=66%, kv_hit=0.28
- adaptive-priming: p50=68ms, p95=175ms, p99=220ms, qps=390, gpu_util=63%, kv_hit=0.37
- long-timeout: p50=44ms, p95=340ms, p99=1200ms, qps=450, gpu_util=75%, kv_hit=0.09

Quick takeaways:
- Warm probes reduce tail substantially (prewarm-eager vs baseline), but eager approach wastes ~4-6% cycles in low-burst runs.
- Staggering prewarm offsets hits a good sweet spot: maintains cache effectiveness while smoothing cluster inflight; big p99 wins with modest cost.
- Adaptive priming (detect miss spikes, then send targeted small prefix requests) gives best p99 vs cost tradeoff in these traces; implementation complexity moderate.
- Increasing batch timeout aggressively improves p50 and throughput at the expense of tail under sudden synchronized opens — avoid as blanket default.

Micro-observations / anomalies:
- On run #2 with adaptive-priming, one shard showed sustained 40% higher GPU mem allocs; digging into request shape showed several priming requests were much longer (prompt dumps). Need guard on priming token-length.
- Queue depth histograms show small population of requests experiencing >3x latency because they missed the opportunistic coalesce window (race with batch flush).

Open action items:
- Add a max-priming-tokens cap (suggest 32) and re-run adaptive-priming. (Priya)
- Instrument batcher to emit "coalesce-missed" counter and trace examples. (Maya)
- Run a longer 1h sweep at 8x scale to measure cost impact of staggered prewarm in diurnal pattern. (me)
- Draft a short note for infra team: suggest a prewarm feature flag that supports stagger windows and priming token cap.

Notes to self: keep the priming payload tiny, prefer prefix-only priming (no full prompt). Consider a heuristic: only prime if recent kv_hit < threshold AND expected client concurrency > 32.

Thoughts on productionization (sketch):
- Operator-level knobs: prewarm_enabled, prewarm_window_ms, priming_tokens_cap, priming_sample_rate, batch_timeout_ms
- Telemetry: priming_count, priming_success_rate (kv_hit delta), coalesce_missed_rate, tail_latency_by_shard

Links / references: INF-1298 experiment ticket, PR 487.

Random scratch ideas: what if clients emitted a tiny 1-token ping signed with metric label during idle->active transition? Low-cost and lets server decide whether to prime. Worth A/Bing.

End of notes. Will iterate after the priming-token-cap test (next run 2025-08-07).
